newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy must continue restoring finances to health.
newsitem.headline: Italy must continue restoring finances to health.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy's efforts to restore public finances to health must not be interrupted otherwise the country risked distancing itself from Europe.

His ministry, in a resume of Italy's economic situation issued on Friday, said "the progress made in the consolidation of public accounts and in the disinflation of the productive system cannot be interrupted.
"Otherwise this would lead to a drawing away from Europe and the return to a situation of instability which would trigger (an upturn in inflation)", the statement said.

It said the vigour of budgetary measures for this year would result in "considerable progress in terms of reducing the deficit in 1997, greater progress than made in the past and greater progress than that made by other European countries.
"There are solid bases for full participation in Europe and for a balanced development of the economy," the Treasury said.

The statement added that in 1997 "growth of the Italian economy will remain weak, little above that seen in 1996", when GDP rose 0.7 percent, but the Treasury confirmed this year's growth target of 1.2 percent.
